eli: quick heads-up — bringing Marlin-11B (Qwen tokenizer) into llama-serving for int4 experiments. shortbench fine but long-context QA and rerank look noisy >2k tokens.

sam: summary of failure mode? token splits or hallucinations?

eli: both. see example below. conversion used qwen->llama mapper + pack-order=chunked. quantize int4 calib=200k. runtime flags: --kvprefetch=on --rotary-head-scale=on. short answers ok, long ones append small directive fragments or split words mid-token.

eli: repro commands:
```bash
python convert_qwen_to_llama.py --in marlin11b.qwen --out marlin11b.llama --token-map nfkc-normalize
python quantize.py --model marlin11b.llama --dtype int4 --calib 200000 --pack-order chunked
redwood serve --model marlin11b.int4 --dev --kvprefetch=on --rotary-head-scale=on --profile long-qa
```

yasmin: paste a concrete diff (float32 vs int4) if you have one.

eli: trimmed example:
float32: "...the migration will proceed after validation of checksums and a canary pass."
int4:   "...the migration will proceed after validation of checksums and a canary pass.
Action: see Appendix B"

eli: also a token-split case: float32 -> "namespaces" ; int4 -> "name
spaces" (newline inserted).

sam: did you try fake-quant sim to isolate packing vs numeric quant error?

eli: fake-quant sim reproduces the issue when pack-order=chunked. switching to pack-order=head-contiguous fixes sim. disabling --rotary-head-scale also mostly removes the directive append but not the newline token-split.

yasmin: that suggests two things: 1) pack-order/layout mismatch causing rotary phase swaps for grouped heads (explains directives in long context via KV cache misalignment), 2) packing stride/padding bug shifting embedding rows (explains token-split/newline).

ops-bot: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-dev/model-artifacts/marlin11b/debug-pack/ (sha256: e3f4a1b7).

sam: can you run two quick diagnostics: (A) per-head rotary-base max-abs-diff between original and deserialized under both pack-orders, (B) per-embedding-row sha1 hash roundtrip check. small snippets exist in our convert-tooling.

eli: ran both. (A) with chunked packing diffs spike on heads [10,11,26,27], (B) embedding-row mismatches at indices that are multiples of 64 (pack stride). token-id histogram check shows a tiny cluster of tokens containing ZWJ/ZWJ-like sequences shifted by +1 occasionally.

yasmin: so ZWJ/normalization plus pack stride/padding interaction can create off-by-one row moves when memmove uses computed sizes based on token counts that differ after normalization. nasty.

sam: remediation options: 1) make packer emit header metadata (head_layout, pack_stride, token_map_hash, crc_rotary, crc_embed_rows) so runtime can validate & remap on load; 2) change packer default to runtime-canonical head-contiguous layout and re-pack artifacts; 3) add conversion smoke tests: per-head rotary alignment and per-row embedding hash roundtrip; 4) fix normalizer to stabilise ZWJ/emoji to avoid id-space shrinkage surprises.

eli: i'm drafting a small patch to write head_layout and a crc32 for rotary+embed tables and to add the per-row hash check to conversion. opening RI-2404 and will tag eng-runtime + tokenizers.

ci-bot: build 5120 triggered: tests/convert::marlin-pack-smoke started.

yasmin: once CI green we should re-run long-qa and rerank suites on repacked int4 artifacts. if header fixes the runtime load path we can schedule small backfill for recent conversions. also add a short long-context smoke (50 docs) to conversion CI to catch KV-cache drift.

eli: thanks — will follow up here after CI results and overnight eval. :spiral_calendar:
